title: Design a Translation Screen State Architecture
prompt: Design client state for a translation screen with source/target language pickers, input, result, swap, clear, and an asynchronous translation engine. Preserve blank and trailing-line semantics, avoid calling the engine for empty input, and avoid stale results when requests race. Cover state transitions, cache keys, cancellation, accessibility, and testability; rendering framework code is out of scope.

response.placeholder: Write the screen state and transition rules first, including what swap does to an in-flight request.
response.reference_answer:
## State and transitions
Keep source language, target language, raw input, displayed result, request generation, loading/error state, and an in-memory cache. Clear resets input/result and cancels the active generation. Swap exchanges languages, invalidates any request tied to the old pair, and either preserves input as explicitly documented or clears stale result.

## Text semantics
Empty input never calls the engine. Whitespace is still user-visible and clearable; preserve blank and trailing lines when sending/receiving text. Tag every request with a generation and accept a completion only if it matches current input/language state.

## Cache and UX
Cache by exact `(input, source, target)` tuple, not normalized text that would erase formatting. Disable or serialize conflicting actions during a request, expose retry/error accessibly, and make fake-engine tests deterministic with an injected dispatcher.

## Progressive Hints
1. Raw text and rendered result are separate state.
2. A late response is not automatically current.
3. Formatting is part of the cache key.
